Q: Virtual Python environment broke after upgrading Ubuntu 15.10 (Wily Werewolf) to Ubuntu 16.04 (Xenial Xerus) A:

I fixed this by installing the minimum working Python 3.4 so that my virtualenv worked well enough to get the list of packages, then made a new one with Python 3.5... as follows:

Get Python 3.4 minimal packages:

wget http://launchpadlibrarian.net/221250032/python3.4-minimal_3.4.3-1ubuntu1~14.04.3_amd64.deb
wget http://launchpadlibrarian.net/221250033/libpython3.4-minimal_3.4.3-1ubuntu1~14.04.3_amd64.deb
sudo dpkg -i --force-breaks libpython3.4-minimal_3.4.3-1ubuntu1~14.04.3_amd64.deb
sudo dpkg -i python3.4-minimal_3.4.3-1ubuntu1~14.04.3_amd64.deb

My virtualenv is here: ~/virtualenv/example

Get the list of packages in your virtualenv (which should now work well enough for this, but might not do other things properly):

source ~/virtualenv/example/bin/activate
pip freeze > /tmp/requirements.txt
deactivate

Get rid of Python 3.4, to return to Ubuntu 16.04's preferred state:

sudo dpkg --purge python3.4-minimal
sudo dpkg --force-depends --purge libpython3.4-minimal

Make a new virtualenv with the right packages:

virtualenv -p python3.5 example
source ~/virtualenv/example/bin/activate
pip install -r /tmp/requirements.txt

That should now work, with all your old packages but in Python 3.5. Should...

See also Upgrade Python in a virtual environment.

Q: Chinese vertical text renders incorrectly after rotation with Graphics.DrawString in WinForms A:

Remove StringFormatFlags.DirectionVertical and change the rotation angle to 270 degrees to get your desired output.

DirectionVertical will draw the text vertically, if the characters are rotated or not will depend on the specific language. So Chinese characters will not be rotated, but numbers and latin text will. Then g.RotateTransform(180f) will rotate all of the text, causing all the Chinese characters to be upside down.

Use g.RotateTransform(270f) without any DirectionVertical flag to draw the entire string as it is, but rotated.

Q: Wordpress Vs Core PHP for Sport club A:

If you can find wordpress plugins which provide those various features then that would certainly save you some time compared to developing it from scratch.

You might also want to consider if there are SaaS platforms out there which your club can use for a reasonable price to manage bookings etc. Every club is different of course, but equally "booking a tennis court" or "buying a t-shirt" or whatever it might be is probably quite a standard process for most organisations.

If you use a sufficiently flexible platform you may find you can make it work for you without the headache of building, maintaining and enhancing a completely custom platform (which, you have to remember, may outlast your own personal membership of the club or interest in developing it. Being the only person who can support a whole platform is not always fun - I speak from hard-won experience here!).

Q: Is it possible to display csv file as a table in Markdown? A:

If you just want to make a nice table from the CSV file and you do not mind doing some copying, you can try this workaround, which is not an answer to your question but worth mentioning.

Load the CSV for example in a sheet and copy the HTML output, and then paste from clipboard where you want to show it. Often, where markdown works, also HTML works, and then you would not need to code it in markdown.

If you can save the table in HTML right away, you can even skip the CSV step, but I guess you have to begin with the CSV file.
